198	 104  def blocked_local_attention(
199	 105      batch: int,
200	 106      length: int,
201	 107      num_heads: int,
202	 108      *,
203	 109      window: int,
204	 110      causal: bool,
205	 111      block: int,
206	 112      attention_mask: mx.array | None = None,
207	 113  ) -> Attend:
208	 114      """Sliding-window attention over a full sequence in O(L * window).
209	 115  
210	 116      Queries are split into blocks of ``block`` rows. Block ``i`` attends to the
211	 117      contiguous key span that any of its rows can see: ``[i*block - w, (i+1)*block + w)``
212	 118      for the bidirectional window and ``[i*block - w + 1, (i+1)*block)`` for the causal
213	 119      one. The spans overlap, so they are exposed as an ``as_strided`` view of the padded
214	 120      keys (no copy) and fed to the fused SDPA kernel as a ``(B*H, n_blocks, span, D)``
215	 121      batch. The exact window/padding mask is applied inside each span, so the result
216	 122      equals dense masked attention up to float summation order.
217	 123      """
218	 124      n_blocks = math.ceil(length / block)
219	 125      padded = n_blocks * block
220	 126      left = window if not causal else window - 1
221	 127      right = (padded - length) + (0 if causal else window)
222	 128      span = block + left + (0 if causal else window)
223	 129      total = left + length + right  # padded key length (row stride of the strided view)
224	 130  
225	 131      # Absolute key position for (block i, slot j) and query position for (block i, row r).
226	 132      k_pos = mx.arange(n_blocks)[:, None] * block - left + mx.arange(span)[None, :]
227	 133      q_pos = mx.arange(n_blocks)[:, None] * block + mx.arange(block)[None, :]
228	 134      rel = k_pos[:, None, :] - q_pos[:, :, None]  # (n_blocks, block, span)
229	 135      mask = (rel <= 0) & (rel > -window) if causal else mx.abs(rel) <= window
230	 136      key_ok = (k_pos >= 0) & (k_pos < length)  # (n_blocks, span)
231	 137      if attention_mask is None:
232	 138          mask = (mask & key_ok[:, None, :])[None]  # (1, n_blocks, block, span)
233	 139      else:
234	 140          valid = attention_mask.astype(mx.bool_)
235	 141          k_valid = mx.take(valid, mx.clip(k_pos, 0, length - 1).reshape(-1), axis=1)
236	 142          k_valid = k_valid.reshape(batch, n_blocks, 1, span) & key_ok[None, :, None, :]
237	 143          q_valid = mx.pad(valid, [(0, 0), (0, padded - length)]).reshape(batch, n_blocks, block, 1)
238	 144          mask = mask[None] & (k_valid | ~q_valid)  # (B, n_blocks, block, span)
239	 145          mask = mx.broadcast_to(mask[:, None], (batch, num_heads, n_blocks, block, span))
240	 146          mask = mask.reshape(batch * num_heads, n_blocks, block, span)
241	 147  
242	 148      def windows(x):
243	 149          B, H, _, D = x.shape
244	 150          x = mx.pad(x, [(0, 0), (0, 0), (left, right), (0, 0)])
245	 151          return mx.as_strided(x, (B * H, n_blocks, span, D), (total * D, block * D, D, 1))
246	 152  
247	 153      def attend(q, k, v, scale):
248	 154          B, H, L, D = q.shape
249	 155          qb = mx.pad(q, [(0, 0), (0, 0), (0, padded - L), (0, 0)]).reshape(B * H, n_blocks, block, D)
250	 156          out = mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention(qb, windows(k), windows(v), scale=scale, mask=mask)
251	 157          out = out.reshape(B, H, padded, D)[:, :, :L]
252	 158          return out.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, L, -1)
253	 159  
254	 160      return attend

263	   5  stores the last ``window - 1`` keys and returns them concatenated with the new ones,
264	   6  which is exactly the set a decoder sliding layer (``q - window < k <= q``) can see
265	   7  for a single new token. Keys are cached after RoPE.
266	   8  """

274	  16      step = 256
275	  17

277	  19          self.keys: mx.array | None = None
278	  20          self.values: mx.array | None = None
279	  21          self.offset = 0
280	  22  
281	  23      def kv_start(self) -> int:
282	  24          """Absolute position of the first key that ``update_and_fetch`` will return."""
283	  25          return 0
284	  26  
285	  27      def update_and_fetch(self, keys: mx.array, values: mx.array) -> tuple[mx.array, mx.array]:
286	  28          prev, n = self.offset, keys.shape[2]
287	  29          if self.keys is None or prev + n > self.keys.shape[2]:
288	  30              B, H, _, D = keys.shape
289	  31              capacity = ((prev + n + self.step - 1) // self.step) * self.step
290	  32              new_k = mx.zeros((B, H, capacity, D), keys.dtype)
291	  33              new_v = mx.zeros((B, H, capacity, D), values.dtype)
292	  34              if self.keys is not None:
293	  35                  new_k[..., :prev, :] = self.keys[..., :prev, :]
294	  36                  new_v[..., :prev, :] = self.values[..., :prev, :]
295	  37              self.keys, self.values = new_k, new_v
296	  38          self.keys[..., prev : prev + n, :] = keys
297	  39          self.values[..., prev : prev + n, :] = values
298	  40          self.offset += n
299	  41          return self.keys[..., : self.offset, :], self.values[..., : self.offset, :]

303	  45      def __init__(self, window: int):
304	  46          self.keep = window - 1
305	  47          self.keys: mx.array | None = None
306	  48          self.values: mx.array | None = None
307	  49          self.offset = 0
308	  50  
309	  51      def kv_start(self) -> int:
310	  52          return self.offset - (0 if self.keys is None else self.keys.shape[2])
311	  53  
312	  54      def update_and_fetch(self, keys: mx.array, values: mx.array) -> tuple[mx.array, mx.array]:
313	  55          self.offset += keys.shape[2]

315	  57              keys = mx.concatenate([self.keys, keys], axis=2)
316	  58              values = mx.concatenate([self.values, values], axis=2)
317	  59          start = max(keys.shape[2] - self.keep, 0)
318	  60          self.keys, self.values = keys[:, :, start:], values[:, :, start:]

   1  """Attention masks and attention kernels.
   2  
   3  Mask semantics follow ``transformers.masking_utils`` (eager/sdpa paths):
   4  
   5  * encoder full layers:    every key, minus padded keys;
   6  * encoder sliding layers: ``|q - k| <= w`` (``sliding_window_bidirectional_overlay``);
   7  * decoder full layers:    ``k <= q``;
   8  * decoder sliding layers: ``q - w < k <= q`` (``sliding_window_overlay`` + causal).
   9  
  10  ``w`` is ``config.sliding_window`` (= ``local_attention // 2``). A 2D ``attention_mask``
  11  (1 = token, 0 = padding) indexed by absolute position removes padded keys. Rows of
  12  padded *queries* ignore the padding mask instead of being fully masked, so they stay
  13  finite (HF fills them with a uniform softmax over ``finfo.min``); their values are
  14  never read by real tokens.
  15  
  16  Every mask is built once per forward call per layer type and closed over by an
  17  ``attend(q, k, v, scale) -> (B, Lq, H*D)`` callable that each layer calls.
  18  """
  19  
  20  from __future__ import annotations
  21  
  22  import math
  23  from collections.abc import Callable
  24  
  25  import mlx.core as mx
  26  
  27  Attend = Callable[[mx.array, mx.array, mx.array, float], mx.array]
  28  Mask = mx.array | str | None
  29  
  30  # Below this length the dense masked kernel is as fast as the blocked one.
  31  BLOCKED_MIN_LENGTH = 512
  32  
  33  
  34  def use_blocked(mode: str, length: int, window: int) -> bool:
  35      if mode == "dense":
  36          return False
  37      if mode == "blocked":
  38          return True
  39      if mode != "auto":
  40          raise ValueError(f"local_attention must be 'auto', 'dense' or 'blocked', got {mode!r}")
  41      return length >= BLOCKED_MIN_LENGTH and length > 4 * window
  42  
  43  
  44  def build_mask(
  45      q_start: int,
  46      q_len: int,
  47      kv_start: int,
  48      kv_len: int,
  49      *,
  50      causal: bool,
  51      window: int | None,
  52      attention_mask: mx.array | None = None,
  53  ) -> Mask:
  54      """Boolean mask (True = attend) broadcastable to ``(B, H, q_len, kv_len)``.
  55  
  56      Queries sit at absolute positions ``[q_start, q_start + q_len)`` and keys at
  57      ``[kv_start, kv_start + kv_len)``. Returns ``None`` when nothing is masked and
  58      ``"causal"`` when the plain lower-right causal mask is exact.
  59      """
  60      q_last, kv_last = q_start + q_len - 1, kv_start + kv_len - 1
  61      if causal:
  62          need_causal = kv_last > q_start
  63          need_window = window is not None and kv_start <= q_last - window
  64      else:
  65          need_causal = False
  66          need_window = window is not None and max(q_last - kv_start, kv_last - q_start) > window
  67  
  68      if attention_mask is None:
  69          if not (need_causal or need_window):
  70              return None
  71          if need_causal and not need_window and kv_last == q_last:
  72              return "causal"
  73  
  74      qi = mx.arange(q_start, q_start + q_len)[:, None]
  75      ki = mx.arange(kv_start, kv_start + kv_len)[None, :]
  76      mask = None
  77      if need_causal:
  78          mask = ki <= qi
  79      if need_window:
  80          in_window = (ki > qi - window) if causal else (mx.abs(qi - ki) <= window)
  81          mask = in_window if mask is None else mask & in_window
  82      if attention_mask is not None:
  83          valid = attention_mask.astype(mx.bool_)
  84          key_ok = valid[:, None, None, kv_start : kv_start + kv_len]
  85          if mask is None:
  86              # Unrestricted attention: every query row sees all real keys, so a
  87              # (B, 1, 1, kv_len) key mask is enough (rows with no real key at all
  88              # are let through instead of producing NaN).
  89              return key_ok | ~mx.any(key_ok, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
  90          query_pad = ~valid[:, None, q_start : q_start + q_len, None]
  91          mask = mask & (key_ok | query_pad)
  92      return mask
  93  
  94  
  95  def dense_attention(mask: Mask) -> Attend:
  96      def attend(q, k, v, scale):
  97          B, _, L, _ = q.shape
  98          out = mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, scale=scale, mask=mask)
  99          return out.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, L, -1)
 100  
 101      return attend
 102  
 103  
 104  def blocked_local_attention(
 105      batch: int,
 106      length: int,
 107      num_heads: int,
 108      *,
 109      window: int,
 110      causal: bool,
 111      block: int,
 112      attention_mask: mx.array | None = None,
 113  ) -> Attend:
 114      """Sliding-window attention over a full sequence in O(L * window).
 115  
 116      Queries are split into blocks of ``block`` rows. Block ``i`` attends to the
 117      contiguous key span that any of its rows can see: ``[i*block - w, (i+1)*block + w)``
 118      for the bidirectional window and ``[i*block - w + 1, (i+1)*block)`` for the causal
 119      one. The spans overlap, so they are exposed as an ``as_strided`` view of the padded
 120      keys (no copy) and fed to the fused SDPA kernel as a ``(B*H, n_blocks, span, D)``
 121      batch. The exact window/padding mask is applied inside each span, so the result
 122      equals dense masked attention up to float summation order.
 123      """
 124      n_blocks = math.ceil(length / block)
 125      padded = n_blocks * block
 126      left = window if not causal else window - 1
 127      right = (padded - length) + (0 if causal else window)
 128      span = block + left + (0 if causal else window)
 129      total = left + length + right  # padded key length (row stride of the strided view)
 130  
 131      # Absolute key position for (block i, slot j) and query position for (block i, row r).
 132      k_pos = mx.arange(n_blocks)[:, None] * block - left + mx.arange(span)[None, :]
 133      q_pos = mx.arange(n_blocks)[:, None] * block + mx.arange(block)[None, :]
 134      rel = k_pos[:, None, :] - q_pos[:, :, None]  # (n_blocks, block, span)
 135      mask = (rel <= 0) & (rel > -window) if causal else mx.abs(rel) <= window
 136      key_ok = (k_pos >= 0) & (k_pos < length)  # (n_blocks, span)
 137      if attention_mask is None:
 138          mask = (mask & key_ok[:, None, :])[None]  # (1, n_blocks, block, span)
 139      else:
 140          valid = attention_mask.astype(mx.bool_)
 141          k_valid = mx.take(valid, mx.clip(k_pos, 0, length - 1).reshape(-1), axis=1)
 142          k_valid = k_valid.reshape(batch, n_blocks, 1, span) & key_ok[None, :, None, :]
 143          q_valid = mx.pad(valid, [(0, 0), (0, padded - length)]).reshape(batch, n_blocks, block, 1)
 144          mask = mask[None] & (k_valid | ~q_valid)  # (B, n_blocks, block, span)
 145          mask = mx.broadcast_to(mask[:, None], (batch, num_heads, n_blocks, block, span))
 146          mask = mask.reshape(batch * num_heads, n_blocks, block, span)
 147  
 148      def windows(x):
 149          B, H, _, D = x.shape
 150          x = mx.pad(x, [(0, 0), (0, 0), (left, right), (0, 0)])
 151          return mx.as_strided(x, (B * H, n_blocks, span, D), (total * D, block * D, D, 1))
 152  
 153      def attend(q, k, v, scale):
 154          B, H, L, D = q.shape
 155          qb = mx.pad(q, [(0, 0), (0, 0), (0, padded - L), (0, 0)]).reshape(B * H, n_blocks, block, D)
 156          out = mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention(qb, windows(k), windows(v), scale=scale, mask=mask)
 157          out = out.reshape(B, H, padded, D)[:, :, :L]
 158          return out.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, L, -1)
 159  
 160      return attend

   1  """KV caches for the decoder.
   2  
   3  ``KVCache`` (full-attention layers) keeps every key in a buffer that grows in steps,
   4  written in place. ``SlidingKVCache`` mirrors HF's ``DynamicSlidingWindowLayer``: it
   5  stores the last ``window - 1`` keys and returns them concatenated with the new ones,
   6  which is exactly the set a decoder sliding layer (``q - window < k <= q``) can see
   7  for a single new token. Keys are cached after RoPE.
   8  """
   9  
  10  from __future__ import annotations
  11  
  12  import mlx.core as mx
  13  
  14  
  15  class KVCache:
  16      step = 256
  17  
  18      def __init__(self):
  19          self.keys: mx.array | None = None
  20          self.values: mx.array | None = None
  21          self.offset = 0
  22  
  23      def kv_start(self) -> int:
  24          """Absolute position of the first key that ``update_and_fetch`` will return."""
  25          return 0
  26  
  27      def update_and_fetch(self, keys: mx.array, values: mx.array) -> tuple[mx.array, mx.array]:
  28          prev, n = self.offset, keys.shape[2]
  29          if self.keys is None or prev + n > self.keys.shape[2]:
  30              B, H, _, D = keys.shape
  31              capacity = ((prev + n + self.step - 1) // self.step) * self.step
  32              new_k = mx.zeros((B, H, capacity, D), keys.dtype)
  33              new_v = mx.zeros((B, H, capacity, D), values.dtype)
  34              if self.keys is not None:
  35                  new_k[..., :prev, :] = self.keys[..., :prev, :]
  36                  new_v[..., :prev, :] = self.values[..., :prev, :]
  37              self.keys, self.values = new_k, new_v
  38          self.keys[..., prev : prev + n, :] = keys
  39          self.values[..., prev : prev + n, :] = values
  40          self.offset += n
  41          return self.keys[..., : self.offset, :], self.values[..., : self.offset, :]
  42  
  43  
  44  class SlidingKVCache:
  45      def __init__(self, window: int):
  46          self.keep = window - 1
  47          self.keys: mx.array | None = None
  48          self.values: mx.array | None = None
  49          self.offset = 0
  50  
  51      def kv_start(self) -> int:
  52          return self.offset - (0 if self.keys is None else self.keys.shape[2])
  53  
  54      def update_and_fetch(self, keys: mx.array, values: mx.array) -> tuple[mx.array, mx.array]:
  55          self.offset += keys.shape[2]
  56          if self.keys is not None:
  57              keys = mx.concatenate([self.keys, keys], axis=2)
  58              values = mx.concatenate([self.values, values], axis=2)
  59          start = max(keys.shape[2] - self.keep, 0)
  60          self.keys, self.values = keys[:, :, start:], values[:, :, start:]
  61          return keys, values

  18  class EttinDecoder(nn.Module):
  19      """Causal LM with full and sliding-window layers and an optional KV cache.
  20  
  21      ``attention_mask`` follows HF: shape ``(B, past + L)``, 1 = token, 0 = padding.
  22      Positions are ``arange(L) + past`` (HF's default when no ``position_ids`` are given).
  23      ``local_attention`` and ``rope`` are as in ``EttinEncoder``.
  24      """

  26      def __init__(self, config: EttinConfig, local_attention: str = "auto", rope: str = "precise"):
  27          super().__init__()
  28          if not config.is_decoder:
  29              raise ValueError(f"EttinDecoder needs model_type 'modernbert-decoder', got {config.model_type!r}")
  30          self.config = config
  31          self.local_attention = local_attention
  32          self.rope = rope
  33          self.model = Backbone(config)
  34          self.lm_head = PredictionHead(config)
  35          self.decoder = LMDecoder(config)
  36          object.__setattr__(self, "_compiled", None)
  37  
  38      def make_cache(self) -> Cache:
  39          w = self.config.sliding_window
  40          return [SlidingKVCache(w) if t == SLIDING else KVCache() for t in self.config.layer_types]
  41  
  42      def attention_plan(
  43          self, batch: int, length: int, attention_mask: mx.array | None, cache: Cache | None
  44      ) -> dict[str, Attend]:
  45          cfg = self.config
  46          types = cfg.layer_types
  47          offset = cache[0].offset if cache else 0
  48          if attention_mask is not None and attention_mask.shape[-1] != offset + length:
  49              raise ValueError(f"attention_mask covers {attention_mask.shape[-1]} positions, expected {offset + length}")
  50          plan = {}
  51          if FULL in types:
  52              mask = build_mask(offset, length, 0, offset + length, causal=True, window=None, attention_mask=attention_mask)
  53              plan[FULL] = dense_attention(mask)
  54          if SLIDING in types:
  55              w = cfg.sliding_window
  56              kv_start = cache[types.index(SLIDING)].kv_start() if cache else 0
  57              if offset == 0 and use_blocked(self.local_attention, length, w):
  58                  plan[SLIDING] = blocked_local_attention(
  59                      batch, length, cfg.num_attention_heads,
  60                      window=w, causal=True, block=w, attention_mask=attention_mask,
  61                  )
  62              else:
  63                  mask = build_mask(
  64                      offset, length, kv_start, offset + length - kv_start,
  65                      causal=True, window=w, attention_mask=attention_mask,
  66                  )
  67                  plan[SLIDING] = dense_attention(mask)
  68          return plan
  69  
  70      def hidden_states(
  71          self, input_ids: mx.array, attention_mask: mx.array | None = None, cache: Cache | None = None
  72      ) -> mx.array:
  73          B, L = input_ids.shape
  74          offset = cache[0].offset if cache else 0
  75          rope = make_rope(self.rope, self.config, offset, L)
  76          return self.model(input_ids, self.attention_plan(B, L, attention_mask, cache), rope, cache)
  77  
  78      def logits(self, hidden: mx.array) -> mx.array:
  79          return self.decoder(self.lm_head(hidden), self.model.embeddings.tok_embeddings.weight)
  80  
  81      def _forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask=None, cache=None, logits_to_keep=0):
  82          hidden = self.hidden_states(input_ids, attention_mask, cache)
  83          if logits_to_keep:
  84              hidden = hidden[:, -logits_to_keep:]
  85          return self.logits(hidden)
  86  
  87      def compile(self) -> EttinDecoder:
  88          """Route cache-less forward calls through ``mx.compile``.
  89  
  90          Calls with a cache stay eager: the cache is Python-side state that changes
  91          shape every step, so a compiled decode step would retrace every token.
  92          """
  93          me = weakref.ref(self)  # no self-reference cycle: `del model` frees the weights at once
  94          compiled = {
  95              "forward": mx.compile(lambda ids: me()._forward(ids)),
  96              "forward_mask": mx.compile(lambda ids, m: me()._forward(ids, m)),
  97          }
  98          object.__setattr__(self, "_compiled", compiled)
  99          return self
 100  
 101      def __call__(
 102          self,
 103          input_ids: mx.array,
 104          attention_mask: mx.array | None = None,
 105          cache: Cache | None = None,
 106          logits_to_keep: int = 0,
 107      ) -> mx.array:
 108          if self._compiled is None or cache is not None or logits_to_keep:
 109              return self._forward(input_ids, attention_mask, cache, logits_to_keep)
 110          if attention_mask is None:
 111              return self._compiled["forward"](input_ids)
 112          return self._compiled["forward_mask"](input_ids, attention_mask)

  15  class EttinEncoder(nn.Module):
  16      """Bidirectional encoder with an MLM head.
  17  
  18      ``encode`` returns the last hidden state (after ``final_norm``), ``__call__`` the MLM
  19      logits. Inputs are ``(B, L)`` token ids plus an optional right-padding mask
  20      (1 = token, 0 = pad). Position ids are ``arange(L)`` regardless of padding, as in HF.
  21  
  22      ``local_attention`` selects the sliding-layer kernel: ``"dense"`` (masked SDPA over
  23      the whole sequence), ``"blocked"`` (O(L * window)) or ``"auto"``. ``rope`` selects
  24      ``"precise"`` (HF float32 tables) or ``"fast"`` (``mx.fast.rope``).
  25      """
  26  
  27      def __init__(self, config: EttinConfig, local_attention: str = "auto", rope: str = "precise"):
  28          super().__init__()
  29          if config.is_decoder:
  30              raise ValueError(f"EttinEncoder needs model_type 'modernbert', got {config.model_type!r}")
  31          self.config = config
  32          self.local_attention = local_attention
  33          self.rope = rope
  34          self.model = Backbone(config)
  35          self.head = PredictionHead(config)
  36          self.decoder = LMDecoder(config)
  37          # Plain attribute (not a module child): MLX would treat a dict as a subtree.
  38          object.__setattr__(self, "_compiled", None)
  39  
  40      def attention_plan(self, batch: int, length: int, attention_mask: mx.array | None) -> dict[str, Attend]:
  41          cfg = self.config
  42          plan = {}
  43          if FULL in cfg.layer_types:
  44              mask = build_mask(0, length, 0, length, causal=False, window=None, attention_mask=attention_mask)
  45              plan[FULL] = dense_attention(mask)
  46          if SLIDING in cfg.layer_types:
  47              w = cfg.sliding_window
  48              if use_blocked(self.local_attention, length, w):
  49                  plan[SLIDING] = blocked_local_attention(
  50                      batch, length, cfg.num_attention_heads,
  51                      window=w, causal=False, block=w, attention_mask=attention_mask,
  52                  )
  53              else:
  54                  mask = build_mask(0, length, 0, length, causal=False, window=w, attention_mask=attention_mask)
  55                  plan[SLIDING] = dense_attention(mask)
  56          return plan
  57  
  58      def _encode(self, input_ids: mx.array, attention_mask: mx.array | None = None) -> mx.array:
  59          B, L = input_ids.shape
  60          rope = make_rope(self.rope, self.config, 0, L)
  61          return self.model(input_ids, self.attention_plan(B, L, attention_mask), rope)
  62  
  63      def logits(self, hidden: mx.array) -> mx.array:
  64          """MLM logits for (a subset of) hidden states, e.g. only the masked positions."""
  65          return self.decoder(self.head(hidden), self.model.embeddings.tok_embeddings.weight)
  66  
  67      def _forward(self, input_ids: mx.array, attention_mask: mx.array | None = None) -> mx.array:
  68          return self.logits(self._encode(input_ids, attention_mask))
  69  
  70      def compile(self) -> EttinEncoder:
  71          """Route ``encode``/``__call__`` through ``mx.compile`` (one trace per input shape)."""
  72          me = weakref.ref(self)  # no self-reference cycle: `del model` frees the weights at once
  73          compiled = {
  74              "encode": mx.compile(lambda ids: me()._encode(ids)),
  75              "encode_mask": mx.compile(lambda ids, m: me()._encode(ids, m)),
  76              "forward": mx.compile(lambda ids: me()._forward(ids)),
  77              "forward_mask": mx.compile(lambda ids, m: me()._forward(ids, m)),
  78          }
  79          object.__setattr__(self, "_compiled", compiled)
  80          return self
  81  
  82      def encode(self, input_ids: mx.array, attention_mask: mx.array | None = None) -> mx.array:
  83          return self._dispatch("encode", self._encode, input_ids, attention_mask)
  84  
  85      def __call__(self, input_ids: mx.array, attention_mask: mx.array | None = None) -> mx.array:
  86          return self._dispatch("forward", self._forward, input_ids, attention_mask)
  87  
  88      def _dispatch(self, name, fn, input_ids, attention_mask):
  89          if self._compiled is None:
  90              return fn(input_ids, attention_mask)
  91          if attention_mask is None:
  92              return self._compiled[name](input_ids)
  93          return self._compiled[name + "_mask"](input_ids, attention_mask)

 161  @mx.compile
 162  def _rotate(x: mx.array, cos: mx.array, sin: mx.array) -> mx.array:
 163      half = x.shape[-1] // 2
 164      xf = x.astype(mx.float32)
 165      x1, x2 = xf[..., :half], xf[..., half:]
 166      return mx.concatenate([x1 * cos - x2 * sin, x2 * cos + x1 * sin], axis=-1).astype(x.dtype)

 169  def rope_tables(base: float, head_dim: int, offset: int, length: int) -> tuple[mx.array, mx.array]:
 170      """``cos``/``sin`` of shape ``(length, head_dim // 2)`` computed like HF in float32:
 171      ``inv_freq = 1 / base ** (arange(0, d, 2) / d)``, ``angle = position * inv_freq``."""
 172      inv_freq = 1.0 / (base ** (mx.arange(0, head_dim, 2, dtype=mx.float32) / head_dim))
 173      angle = mx.arange(offset, offset + length, dtype=mx.float32)[:, None] * inv_freq[None, :]
 174      return mx.cos(angle), mx.sin(angle)

 177  def make_rope(impl: str, config: EttinConfig, offset: int, length: int) -> dict[str, Callable]:
 178      """One rotate-half RoPE callable per layer type, built once per forward call.
 179  
 180      ``precise`` matches HF's float32 cos/sin tables; ``fast`` uses ``mx.fast.rope``,
 181      whose fast-math trig drifts by ~1e-3 at positions in the thousands (see README).
 182      """
 183      d = config.head_dim
 184      ropes = {}
 185      for layer_type in set(config.layer_types):
 186          base = config.rope_theta[layer_type]
 187          if impl == "fast":
 188              ropes[layer_type] = partial(mx.fast.rope, dims=d, traditional=False, base=base, scale=1.0, offset=offset)
 189          elif impl == "precise":
 190              cos, sin = rope_tables(base, d, offset, length)
 191              ropes[layer_type] = lambda x, cos=cos, sin=sin: _rotate(x, cos, sin)
 192          else:
 193              raise ValueError(f"rope must be one of {ROPE_IMPLS}, got {impl!r}")
 194      return ropes

 185

 190        ``Wqkv(...).view(..., 3, heads, head_dim)``).
 191      """
 192      out: dict[str, mx.array] = {}

 194      for name, w in hf.items():
 195          if name == TIED_KEY and config.tie_word_embeddings:
 196              continue

 198              qkv.setdefault((m[1], m[3]), {})[m[2]] = w

 202          missing = [f"{prefix}.{p}_proj.{kind}" for p in "qkv" if p not in parts]
